mainTopic: How רבי מאיר can count several liabilities for eating one כזית: the rule of איסור כולל and איסור מוסיף, which lets a new prohibition take hold even where an older one already exists.
overview: The גמרא asks whether רבי מאיר's many liabilities for one כזית mean he holds איסור חל על איסור. It answers that he only holds of איסור כולל and איסור מוסיף. It then shows how טומאה, הקדש, נותר and יום הכפורים each add on in this way. Next it asks why the משנה does not add פיגול for a fifth חטאת. After answers about one animal, one limb and a limb following its majority are pushed back, it settles on the משנה speaking of one כזית. The כותבת needed for יום הכפורים is filled out with a kidney (רבי זירא) or dates (רב פפא). רב אדא בר אחא instead counts five חטאות by adding a כזית of פיגול. Six is impossible because the throat holds only two כזיתים at once. The גמרא then tests רפרם's claim that carrying does not apply on יום הכפורים, first from our משנה and then from a ברייתא about the שעיר המשתלח, and finally calls his statement a mistake. A new משנה begins: one act of relations with one's daughter can bring six חטאות.

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר hold that a prohibition can take effect on top of another prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה's long list of liabilities shows that רבי מאיר holds איסור חל על איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Shall we say that רבי מאיר holds that a prohibition takes effect where another prohibition already exists?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by suggesting what רבי מאיר's view in the משנה seems to prove. This sets up the next step, where the suggestion will be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes one person liable many times for one bite. That looks as if רבי מאיר thinks a second prohibition can always land on food that is already forbidden. The גמרא asks whether that is really what he holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggested inference, which is often rejected.
A prohibition taking effect on something that is already forbidden

phrases.english: GEMARA
Shall we say that Rabbi Meir holds
that a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's case of many liabilities for one כזית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר's ruling shows that he holds איסור חל על איסור in general.

steps.title: Not in general, only an inclusive or added prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר does not hold איסור חל על איסור in general, but he does hold of איסור כולל and איסור מוסיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that he does not hold that a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition. But an inclusive prohibition and an added prohibition he does hold of.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רבי מאיר only allows a second prohibition to take hold when it is a broader or expanding kind of prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסור כולל covers new items that were not forbidden before, so it also reaches the item that was already forbidden. An איסור מוסיף adds a new type of restriction (for example, a ban on benefit added to a ban on eating). In both cases the new prohibition takes hold because it is not only repeating the old one.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold (of this idea)
Inclusive prohibition: it forbids more items than before, including this one
Added prohibition: it adds a new kind of restriction on the same item

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר does not hold איסור חל על איסור in general. A second prohibition takes hold only if it is an איסור כולל or an איסור מוסיף.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that רבי מאיר lets any prohibition land on any other. Only these two special types can take effect on food that is already forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key rule that explains every liability in the rest of the sugya.

phrases.english: Granted that a prohibition taking effect on a prohibition
he does not hold of,
an inclusive prohibition and an added prohibition
he does hold of.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְהִי דְּאִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 1 and narrows what רבי מאיר holds.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי מאיר holds איסור חל על איסור as a general rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The many liabilities can be explained by the narrower rule of איסור כולל and איסור מוסיף.

steps.title: Becoming impure adds a prohibition on top of the forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition for a טמא to eat sacrificial meat is an איסור כולל, so it takes hold even on חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: While he was pure, he was forbidden only because of the חלב. Once he became impure, since he is now forbidden even to eat pure pieces of meat, a prohibition is also added to him on the חלב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins applying the rule to the משנה's case. It starts with the person becoming טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he was pure, only the חלב was off limits to him. Once he became טמא, all sacrificial meat became forbidden to him, even permitted pieces. Since this new prohibition covers more than before, it is an איסור כולל, and it also reaches the חלב.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (the new rule applies to these things, it applies to this one too)
Pure, permitted pieces of sacrificial meat

phrases.english: A pure person was originally forbidden
only in the forbidden fat;
he became impure,
since he is forbidden even in pure pieces,

phrases.aramaic: אִיתּוֹסַף בֵּיהּ נָמֵי אִיסּוּרָא עִילָּוֵי חֵלֶב.
phrases.english: a prohibition is also added to him on top of the fat.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָהוֹר, מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא אֲסִיר אֶלָּא בְּחֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of step 2 to the first added prohibition, טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טומאה is an איסור כולל, so it takes effect on חלב.

steps.title: Consecrating the animal adds a ban on benefit
steps.stepSummary: הקדש adds a ban on any benefit, which is an איסור מוסיף, so it also takes hold on the חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חלב was originally forbidden only for eating. Once he consecrated the animal, since a ban on benefit was added to it, that ban was also added regarding the חלב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next prohibition in the case, הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, חלב was only forbidden to eat, and you could still benefit from it in other ways. Consecrating it added a new kind of ban, on all benefit. Because it adds a new type of restriction, it is an איסור מוסיף and takes hold even on the eating.

phrases.english: And the fat was originally forbidden
only in eating;
he consecrated it,
since a prohibition of benefit was added to it,
it was added to it regarding the fat as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחֵלֶב מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא אֲסִיר אֶלָּא בַּאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues listing the added prohibitions; this one is an איסור מוסיף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדש is an איסור מוסיף, so it takes effect on חלב.

steps.title: Becoming leftover adds a ban for the altar too
steps.stepSummary: Consecrated חלב was still fit for the altar. When it became נותר, it became forbidden for the altar too, and that added prohibition also reaches the ordinary person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, it was forbidden only to an ordinary person, but permitted to the Most High. When it became נותר, since a prohibition was added regarding the Most High, it was also added regarding the ordinary person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a point and answers it: the חלב was already forbidden to people, so how can נותר be added? It explains that נותר adds a ban for the altar too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Consecrated חלב is meant to be burned on the altar, so it was still permitted for גבוה. Once it became נותר, it could no longer be offered either. Since נותר adds a new restriction for the altar, it also takes hold for the person who eats it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial meat or fat left past its allowed time

phrases.english: And still, it is forbidden only to an ordinary person
but to the Most High it is permitted;
phrases.notes: Consecrated חלב is supposed to be burned on the altar, so it was still allowed there.

phrases.english: it became leftover,
since a prohibition was added regarding the Most High,
it was added to it regarding the ordinary person too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי לְהֶדְיוֹט הוּא דַּאֲסִיר אֲבָל לְגָבוֹהַּ שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the הקדש of step 4: the חלב is now holy, and נותר adds a further ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נותר adds a ban for the altar, so it also takes effect for the person who eats it.

steps.title: יום הכפורים adds a prohibition even on holy food
steps.stepSummary: יום הכפורים forbids all food, even ordinary חולין, so it is an איסור כולל and also reaches the consecrated נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: When יום הכפורים came upon it, since a prohibition was added regarding ordinary non-holy food, it was added regarding holy food as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list with the last prohibition in the case, יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים even permitted, ordinary food becomes forbidden. Since this prohibition covers new items, it is an איסור כולל. So it also takes hold on the holy food, which was already forbidden many times over.

keyTerms.meaning: The Day of Atonement, when all eating is forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: Each prohibition in the משנה's case takes hold because it is either an איסור כולל (טומאה, יום הכפורים) or an איסור מוסיף (הקדש, נותר). That is how רבי מאיר reaches many liabilities without holding איסור חל על איסור in general.

phrases.english: Yom Kippur took effect on it,

phrases.aramaic: מִיגּוֹ דְּאִיתּוֹסַף בֵּיהּ אִיסּוּר לְגַבֵּי חוּלִּין –
phrases.english: since a prohibition was added regarding non-sacred food,
it was added to it regarding food of the Most High too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of added prohibitions begun in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יום הכפורים is an איסור כולל, so it takes effect even on consecrated נותר.

steps.title: Why not list five sin offerings by adding פיגול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה stops at four חטאות. It could have added a fifth by making the meat פיגול too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the משנה teach five sin offerings, and set the case as one where he ate an olive-bulk of פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. If we are piling prohibitions onto one bite, why not pile on פיגול too and reach five חטאות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3-6 showed how several prohibitions can all take hold on one olive-bulk. If that is true, the משנה should have used the biggest possible list. Since פיגול also brings a חטאת, leaving it out seems strange.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach, meaning 'the משנה should have said'
Sin offerings brought for doing a כרת sin by accident
And let it set up the case as...
An olive-bulk, the minimum amount of eating that counts
A קרבן ruined by the intent to eat or offer it after its proper time

phrases.english: And let it teach: five sin offerings,
phrases.notes: The משנה said one act of eating can bring four חטאות. The גמרא is asking why not five.

phrases.english: and let it set up the case as one
where he ate an olive-bulk of פיגול!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After building the four-prohibition case, the גמרא asks why the משנה did not add a fifth.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's count of four חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If prohibitions can stack, adding פיגול would give five, so stopping at four seems incomplete.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about one animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה only discusses meat from one animal, and one animal cannot be both פיגול and נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is speaking about one animal, not two animals, and you cannot find נותר and פיגול in one animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה limits itself to one animal. In one animal you cannot have both פיגול and נותר, so the fifth חטאת cannot be added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in the משנה needs נותר, which was one of its four prohibitions. Once an animal is פיגול, it is never offered or eaten properly, so it never reaches the stage of being נותר. So within one animal, you must choose one or the other.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot find such a case
קרבן meat left over past its time to be eaten

phrases.english: It is speaking about one animal,
it is not speaking about two animals,
and נותר and פיגול in one animal
you cannot find.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by limiting the case to one animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could have added פיגול to reach five חטאות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Within one animal, פיגול and נותר cannot both exist, so five is impossible.

steps.title: A פיגול limb put on the altar can become נותר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that one animal can have both. A פיגול limb placed on the altar loses its פיגול status and can become נותר, while the rest of the animal stays פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? You can find it, for example where he put a פיגול limb on the altar. Its פיגול status falls away and it becomes נותר, just as עולא said: a פיגול handful of a מנחה that was put on the altar loses its פיגול status and becomes נותר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 8. It brings a case where one animal has both נותר and פיגול, and backs this up with a rule of עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא teaches that once פיגול is placed on the altar, its פיגול status drops away. So that limb is treated like a regular קרבן and can later become נותר. The other limbs of the same animal are still פיגול, so one animal now has both.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the altar

phrases.english: Why not? You can find it

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֶעֱלָה אֵבֶר פִּיגּוּל לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: for example where he brought a פיגול limb up onto the altar,
so that its פיגול status fell away from it
and it became נותר,
and as עולא said:
a פיגול handful that he brought up onto the altar,
its פיגול status falls away from it
and it becomes נותר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְּמָה לָא? מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֶעֱלָה אֵבֶר פִּיגּוּל לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 8's claim that one animal cannot be both פיגול and נותר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נותר and פיגול cannot be found in one animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By עולא's rule, a limb put on the altar loses פיגול and can become נותר while the other limbs stay פיגול, so both exist in one animal.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about one limb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the case further. The משנה is talking about one limb, and one limb cannot be both פיגול and נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is speaking about one limb, not two limbs, and you cannot find נותר and פיגול in one limb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case again, this time from one animal down to one limb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in step 9 needed two limbs: one on the altar (now נותר) and one off it (still פיגול). If the משנה only speaks about a single limb, that limb is either פיגול or נותר, never both.

phrases.english: It is speaking about one limb,
it is not speaking about two limbs,
and נותר and פיגול in one limb
you cannot find.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by narrowing the case from one animal to one limb.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case further (one limb only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא's rule lets one animal hold both פיגול and נותר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a single limb, where both cannot exist.

steps.title: Half a limb on the altar and half off it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that even one limb can have both. If half the limb is on the altar, that half loses its פיגול status and becomes נותר, while the other half stays פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? You can find it, for example where he brought a פיגול limb to the altar and put half of it on the altar and half outside the altar. The half on the altar loses its פיגול status and becomes נותר, as עולא said: a פיגול handful put on the altar loses its פיגול status and becomes נותר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'one limb' answer of step 10. It splits a single limb, half on the altar and half off it, and uses עולא's rule again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's rule works on whatever part actually touches the altar. So the half on the altar becomes able to be נותר, and the half outside stays פיגול. This puts both prohibitions inside one limb. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: עולא's rule is not repeated by mistake. Here it is used for half a limb, to show that even part of a limb can lose its פיגול status.

phrases.english: Why not? You can find it

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֶעֱלָה אֵבֶר פִּיגּוּל לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: for example where he brought a פיגול limb up to the altar,
and he placed half of it on top of the altar,
and half of it outside the altar,
so that for the part on the altar, the פיגול status fell away
and it became נותר,
and as עולא said:
a פיגול handful that he brought up onto the altar,
its פיגול status falls away from it
and it becomes נותר!
phrases.notes: The other half, which never reached the altar, is still פיגול. So one limb now has both.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְּמָה לָא? מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֶעֱלָה אֵבֶר פִּיגּוּל לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ, דְּפַלְגֵיהּ אַנְּחֵיהּ עַל גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10's claim that one limb cannot be both פיגול and נותר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that נותר and פיגול cannot be found in one limb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Placing only half the limb on the altar makes that half able to become נותר by עולא's rule, while the other half stays פיגול.

steps.title: A limb follows its majority
steps.stepSummary: The answerer denies that half a limb can lose its פיגול status. The whole limb follows wherever most of it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. If most of the limb is on the מזבח, treat all of it as on the מזבח. If most of it is outside, treat all of it as outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last question. You cannot split one limb into a פיגול half and a נותר half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said half a limb on the מזבח becomes נותר while the other half stays פיגול. The answer here is that a limb is not split. It goes by its majority, so the whole limb has one status. That means one limb still cannot be both פיגול and נותר, and the answer from step 10 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: throw it, meaning treat it as belonging to

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
if the majority is on the altar –
throw it to the altar,
phrases.notes: He means: treat the whole limb as if it were on the altar.

phrases.english: if the majority is outside –
throw it outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the premise of step 11 to defend the one-limb answer of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the challenger's assumption by using a majority rule for limbs
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Half a limb on the מזבח loses פיגול status while the other half stays פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: A limb follows its majority, so it has one status and cannot be both פיגול and נותר.

steps.title: That would settle רמי בר חמא's open question
steps.stepSummary: If limbs follow the majority, that would answer רמי בר חמא's question, which is treated as unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then you could settle what רמי בר חמא asked: do we follow the majority with limbs or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the answer it just gave. It would solve a question that the גמרא treats as still open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא asked whether a limb follows its majority, and that question was not settled. Step 12 simply assumed that it does. Since we cannot casually settle an open question this way, the step 12 answer is weak.

phrases.english: Resolve that which Rami bar Ḥama asked:

phrases.aramaic: הָלְכוּ בְּאֵבָרִים אַחַר הָרוֹב אוֹ לֹא!
phrases.english: Do we follow the majority with limbs or not!
phrases.notes: The point is that this question was left open, so step 12 cannot just assume an answer to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 12's majority rule because it would decide an unresolved question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that a limb follows its majority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were obvious, רמי בר חמא's question would be answered. Since his question stands unresolved, step 12 cannot rely on it.

steps.title: The משנה is about one כזית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the limb answer. It says the משנה is talking about eating a single כזית, not two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is talking about one כזית. It is not talking about two כזיתים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for why פיגול is not listed. It shrinks the case down to a single olive-size piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if part of a limb could be פיגול and part נותר, a single כזית cannot be both. If the person ate only one כזית, he cannot be liable for both פיגול and נותר. That explains why there is no fifth חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: an olive's volume, the basic amount for liability

phrases.english: Rather, it is talking about one olive-bulk,
it is not talking about two olive-bulks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the limb answer that step 13 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about one limb, which follows its majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about one כזית, which cannot be both פיגול and נותר.

steps.title: יום הכפורים needs more than one כזית
steps.stepSummary: The משנה includes eating on יום הכפורים. That requires a כותבת, which is about two כזיתים, so the משנה must involve more than one כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really not about more? But the משנה lists יום הכפורים, and on יום הכפורים you are only liable for a כותבת, and a כותבת is two כזיתים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the one-כזית answer using a detail from the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of the four חטאות in the משנה is for eating on יום הכפורים. The amount for liability there is a כותבת, a large date, and that is bigger than one כזית. So the משנה's case seems to involve at least two כזיתים, and step 14 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: יום הכפורים, when eating is forbidden
the volume of a large date, the amount for liability on יום הכפורים

phrases.english: And not? But isn't it taught "Yom Kippur,"
and on Yom Kippur it is a large date's volume that makes one liable,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and a large date's volume contains two olive-bulks!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 14's claim that the משנה deals with only one כזית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה's case involves only one כזית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The יום הכפורים חטאת requires a כותבת, about two כזיתים, so the person must have eaten more than one כזית.

steps.title: רבי זירא: a kidney with its fat
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the person ate a kidney with its fat. The fat is one כזית, and the kidney fills out the כותבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: For example, he ate a kidney together with its fat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge. He shows how the משנה can involve only one כזית of the forbidden fat and still reach a כותבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חלב is only one כזית, so the חטאות for the fat apply to that one כזית alone, and it cannot be both פיגול and נותר. The kidney eaten along with it adds enough to reach a כותבת for יום הכפורים. So the one-כזית answer survives.

keyTerms.meaning: its fat, here the forbidden fat on the kidney
for example, such as a case where

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
For example, where he ate a kidney with its fat.
phrases.notes: The fat is the one כזית; the kidney is the extra that brings him up to a כותבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָכַל כּוּלְיָא בְּחֶלְבָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 and saves step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case so the extra volume comes from a different food
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reaching a כותבת means eating two כזיתים of the forbidden fat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one כזית is the forbidden fat. The kidney makes up the rest of the כותבת.

steps.title: רב פפא: he filled it out with dates
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the person ate one כזית of the fat and filled out the כותבת by eating dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: For example, he filled it out with dates.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a second way to answer the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי זירא, רב פפא keeps the forbidden fat at one כזית. Here the extra food is plain dates instead of the kidney. Either way, the fat is one כזית that cannot be both פיגול and נותר, while the total food eaten reaches a כותבת for יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: he filled it out, completed the amount

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has no fifth חטאת for פיגול because it is about eating one כזית of חלב, and one כזית cannot be both פיגול and נותר. The יום הכפורים amount of a כותבת is completed with other food: the kidney according to רבי זירא, or dates according to רב פפא.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
For example, where he filled it out with dates.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּמַלְּיֵיהּ בְּתַמְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different case from רבי זירא to answer the same challenge from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case with a different food to complete the amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כותבת must all be the forbidden fat.
steps.terutzMaskana: One כזית of fat plus dates reaches a כותבת.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אחא's version: five sin offerings with a כזית of פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אחא reads the count as five חטאות and explains the extra one as eating a כזית of פיגול. He does not use the earlier answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אחא taught the count as 'five חטאות.' He explained it as a case where the person also ate a כזית of פיגול. He did not answer the way we answered before.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אחא gives his own answer to the question of how the משנה reaches a כותבת. His answer also brings the count up to five חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי זירא filled the כותבת with a kidney and רב פפא filled it with dates. רב אדא בר אחא fills it with a second forbidden כזית, a piece of פיגול. That adds another חטאת, so he counts five instead of four.

keyTerms.meaning: teaches, meaning he reads the text this way
a קרבן made unfit by a wrong intention about when it would be eaten

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַחָא מַתְנֵי ״חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת״,
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Aha teaches "five sin offerings,"

phrases.aramaic: וּמְתָרֵיץ לַהּ: כְּגוֹן דַּאֲכַל כְּזַיִת פִּיגּוּל,
phrases.english: and he explains it: for example, where he ate an olive-bulk of piggul,
phrases.notes: This is a second כזית eaten together with the forbidden fat. It fills out the כותבת and adds one more חטאת.

phrases.english: and he does not answer like these answers
that we have been answering.
phrases.notes: He means the kidney answer of רבי זירא and the dates answer of רב פפא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third way to solve the כותבת problem, replacing the answers in steps 16-17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case by adding a second forbidden כזית
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כותבת must be filled with something permitted, like a kidney or dates.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is filled with a כזית of פיגול, which raises the count to five חטאות.

steps.title: Why not six, by adding a כזית of blood?
steps.stepSummary: If extra כזיתים can be added, the גמרא asks why the משנה does not add a כזית of דם and count six.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה say 'six חטאות,' and explain it as a case where he also ate a כזית of דם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes רב אדא בר אחא's idea further. If you can add פיגול, why not also add דם and reach six?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we allow more forbidden pieces to be eaten together, there seems to be no limit. The challenge asks why the count stops at five.

keyTerms.meaning: then let it teach (the משנה should have said)
and let us set it up as (explain it as the case of)
blood, which is forbidden to eat and brings a חטאת

phrases.english: But let it teach "six sin offerings,"
and set it up as a case where he ate an olive-bulk of blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 18 by extending its logic.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אחא's count of five
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one extra forbidden כזית may be added, another one (דם) could be added too, giving six.

steps.title: The throat holds only two כזיתים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה speaks of one act of eating, and the חכמים estimated that the throat holds no more than two כזיתים at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about one act of eating, not two. The חכמים estimated that the throat cannot hold more than two כזיתים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a third כזית is impossible within one swallow, so the count stops at five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the חטאות come from a single act of eating. Since the throat holds at most two כזיתים, you can have the fat plus פיגול but not also דם. A third כזית would be a second act of eating.

keyTerms.meaning: the throat, literally the swallowing place

steps.whatToRemember: A single act of eating can include at most two כזיתים, so רב אדא בר אחא's count stops at five.

phrases.english: It is speaking about one act of eating,
it is not speaking about two acts of eating,
and the Sages estimated

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין בֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה מַחֲזִיק יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁנֵי זֵיתִים.
phrases.english: that the throat does not hold more than two olive-bulks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Sets a physical limit on the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any number of forbidden כזיתים could be added to the case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only two כזיתים fit into one act of eating, so six is impossible.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר mention שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר says 'if it was שבת' instead of just 'if he carried it out,' since carrying on יום הכפורים is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says, etc. Let the משנה simply say: 'If he carried it out, he is liable.' Why does it say 'if it was שבת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to רבי מאיר's line in the משנה. It asks why he needs שבת at all, since the case already happens on יום הכפורים. This question sets up רפרם's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלאכה is forbidden on יום הכפורים just as on שבת. So carrying on יום הכפורים alone should already make him liable. Mentioning שבת seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: etc., meaning the rest of the line in the משנה
he carried it out from one domain to another

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says, etc.
phrases.notes: He means רבי מאיר's line in the משנה: if it was שבת and he carried it out, he is liable.

phrases.english: But let it teach: "If he carried it out, he is liable,"
why does it teach "if it was Shabbat"?

steps.triggerLanguage: ונתני אם הוציאו חייב מאי טעמא קתני אם היתה שבת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: רבי מאיר's addition in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה needs the condition of שבת for carrying.

steps.title: רפרם: no עירוב or הוצאה on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רפרם learns from the wording that the laws of עירוב and carrying apply to שבת but not to יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם said: This shows that עירוב and carrying apply to שבת, but there is no עירוב and carrying for יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם answers the question. רבי מאיר needed שבת because carrying on יום הכפורים alone would not make him liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רפרם uses the extra word 'שבת' to draw a legal rule. The prohibition of carrying, and the עירוב that permits it, belong to שבת and not to יום הכפורים. That is why only שבת adds a חטאת here.

keyTerms.meaning: this shows, a rule is being learned from the text
joining of courtyards that permits carrying between them
carrying from one domain to another

steps.confusionAlert: רפרם is not saying יום הכפורים has no מלאכה rules at all. He is only drawing a conclusion about carrying and עירוב.

phrases.english: Rafram said: This is to say:
joining and carrying apply to Shabbat,
but there is no joining and carrying for Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שבת is mentioned because carrying is not forbidden on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Maybe carrying is forbidden on both days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רפרם's proof: maybe carrying is forbidden on יום הכפורים too, and the משנה means he is liable for both שבת and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe עירוב and carrying do apply to יום הכפורים. The משנה means: if it was שבת and he carried it out, he is liable because of both שבת and יום הכפורים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רפרם's reading of the משנה. It offers a different reason why שבת is mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רפרם said שבת is mentioned because carrying on יום הכפורים does not count. The גמרא answers that שבת might be mentioned for a different reason: to show that when both days fall together, carrying makes him liable for both. If so, the משנה proves nothing about יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do you know this
and this is what it is teaching

phrases.english: From where do you know this?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא יֵשׁ עֵירוּב וְהוֹצָאָה לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: Perhaps there is joining and carrying for Yom Kippur,
and this is what it teaches:
If it was Shabbat and he carried it out, he is liable
also because of Shabbat and Yom Kippur!

steps.triggerLanguage: ממאי דלמא יש עירוב והוצאה ליום הכפורים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the inference of step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רפרם's proof from the משנה, not necessarily his rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The mention of שבת can be explained another way: liability for both days at once.

steps.title: Moving רפרם's statement to a ברייתא about the sent-away goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רפרם's statement was really said about a ברייתא that explains the words 'איש עתי' in the פסוק about the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if רפרם said his statement, he said it about this ברייתא: 'And he shall send it with an appointed man.' 'Man' teaches that even a non-כהן may do it. 'Appointed' teaches that it is done even in טומאה and even on שבת. 'Appointed' also means someone prepared ahead of time.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רפרם's proof from our משנה was rejected, the גמרא suggests he actually said it about a different source, and quotes that ברייתא. This sets up רפרם's inference in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains the פסוק about sending away the שעיר המשתלח on יום הכפורים. It learns three things: a זר may lead the goat, it is sent even when the man is טמא or the day is שבת, and the man must be chosen ahead of time. The words 'even on שבת' are what רפרם will focus on.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'appointed man', the person who leads the goat into the desert

phrases.english: Rather, if the statement of רפרם was said,
it was said about this:
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And he shall send it away with an appointed man"
"Man": to make a non-כהן fit for the job.
"Appointed": even in טומאה
and even on שבת.
"Appointed": one who was prepared in advance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אִיתְּמַר דְּרַפְרָם עַל הָדָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 23 rejected רפרם's proof from the משנה, this step moves his statement onto a different source, a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שעיר המשתלח may be led by a זר, is sent even in טומאה and on שבת, and needs a man chosen in advance.

steps.title: רפרם infers that carrying applies to שבת but not to יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא's words 'even on שבת,' רפרם learns that עירוב and carrying apply only to שבת, not to יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא teaches: 'Appointed' means even on שבת. רפרם said: this tells us that the laws of עירוב and carrying apply to שבת, but not to יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם reads the ברייתא closely and draws a rule from it: carrying is a problem only on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leading the goat out to the desert involves carrying. The ברייתא needed to say 'even on שבת' to permit it, but said nothing to permit it on a weekday יום הכפורים. רפרם concludes that on יום הכפורים there was never a carrying problem to begin with.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This tells us', a phrase used to draw a new rule out of a source
Joining of courtyards, which allows carrying between them
Carrying from one domain to another

phrases.english: It teaches: "Appointed": even on שבת.
רפרם said: This tells us
that עירוב and carrying apply to שבת,
but עירוב and carrying do not apply to יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי עִתִּי אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת אָמַר רַפְרָם זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws רפרם's rule out of the ברייתא quoted in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: Carrying is not forbidden on יום הכפורים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's words 'even on שבת' about sending the שעיר המשתלח, with no mention of a permission for יום הכפורים itself.

steps.title: The sent-away goat is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the goat is different, because sending it out is exactly how its מצוה is done on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you learn this? The שעיר המשתלח is different, because this is exactly how it is properly done on יום הכפורים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רפרם's proof by showing that the goat case proves nothing about יום הכפורים in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if carrying is normally forbidden on יום הכפורים, the Torah itself commands sending the goat on that day, so of course it is allowed then. That is why the ברייתא did not need to permit it on יום הכפורים. It only needed to add a special permission for שבת, which is a different day with its own rules.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where?', a challenge asking how the proof works
'It is different', marking a special case
The goat sent away to the desert on יום הכפורים
The proper, valid way of doing something

phrases.english: From where do you prove this?
The sent-away goat is different,
since its proper way on יום הכפורים is exactly this!
phrases.notes: He means the Torah commands sending the goat out on יום הכפורים, so it is allowed that day no matter what.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference רפרם drew in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רפרם's proof from the ברייתא, not necessarily the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The goat is a commanded act of יום הכפורים, so silence about יום הכפורים proves nothing about carrying in general.

steps.title: The statement credited to רפרם is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: Since no source supports it, the גמרא concludes that the statement credited to רפרם was never really said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the statement of רפרם is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on finding a source for רפרם and declares the reported statement an error.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both possible sources, our משנה and the ברייתא, were shown not to prove his rule. So the גמרא concludes the report itself is unreliable, and we cannot rely on it to say carrying is allowed on יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake; a statement that was wrongly reported

steps.whatToRemember: רפרם's rule that עירוב and carrying do not apply on יום הכפורים has no proof, neither from the משנה nor from the ברייתא about the goat, so the גמרא calls the statement a mistake.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not conclude that carrying is forbidden on יום הכפורים either. It only says that the report of רפרם's statement, which claimed carrying does not apply then, is unreliable.

phrases.english: Rather, the statement of רפרם is a mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 26 also fails, the גמרא closes the topic by rejecting the statement entirely.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The statement credited to רפרם is an error and has no support.

steps.title: One act of relations can bring six חטאות
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that one act of ביאה with one's daughter can make a person liable for six separate חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a case where a person has relations once and is liable for six חטאות. How? If a man has relations with his daughter, he can be liable because she is his daughter, his sister, his brother's wife, his father's brother's wife, a married woman, and a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, giving a case where one act breaks six different איסורים at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each איסור is counted separately, so one act can bring several חטאות. The משנה lists six relationships that one woman could have to the man all at once. The גמרא will need to explain how one woman can be all of these together.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering brought for an accidental sin
A woman in her monthly period of impurity

steps.whyThisMatters: It continues the theme of counting how many חטאות one act can bring, like the earlier case of eating.

phrases.english: משנה
There is one who engages in a single act of relations
and is liable for it six חטאות.
How so?
One who has relations with his daughter
is liable for her because she is his daughter,
and his sister, his brother's wife,
and his father's brother's wife,
and a married woman, and a נדה.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ בָּא בִּיאָה אַחַת וְחַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ שֵׁשׁ חַטָּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the רפרם discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One act of relations with one's daughter can bring six separate חטאות, one for each איסור.
